Vision & Values
Our School Vision is:
We aim to achieve the highest academic standards through a rich and well balanced curriculum that is inspiring and engaging. We do this within a happy, safe and stimulating environment.
Our unwavering commitment is to enable children to be confident, respectful and successful global citizens in an ever-changing world now, and in the future.
At Smallberry Green, we celebrate a different value every half-term. They include: Resilience, Optimism, Respect, Curiosity, Inclusion and Confidence.
The Values at Smallberry Green – our school song
Miss Vandervelden has written us a song to help us celebrate and remember our values at Smallberry Green. We are enjoying singing and performing this in our school.
British Values
At Smallberry Green, our vision is to create an excellent and inclusive school community where children are proud of their achievements and excel in their learning. This provides a secure foundation for our work ensuring the understanding and practice of British Values are embedded in every aspect of our school life. We have an obligation to ensure that our children learn about these values and that they practice them through the opportunities we offer at our school.
What we do and plan to do
At Smallberry Green we uphold and teach pupils about British Values which are defined as:
These values are taught explicitly through Personal, Social, Health and Emotional (PSHE), and Religious Education (RE). We also teach British Values through planning and delivering a broad and balanced curriculum.
The school takes opportunities to actively promote British Values through daily reflections and whole school systems and structures such as electing and running a successful School Council. We also actively promote British Values through ensuring that our curriculum planning and delivery includes real opportunities for exploring these values.
Democracy
Rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect
Democracy:
The school council is elected through a democratic process using class pupil votes. During these elections, pupils are provided with the opportunity to learn how to argue and persuade. The school council gives every pupil a voice and supports the organisation of pupil surveys and questionnaires.
Throughout the curriculum, children are given opportunities to debate their ideas and thoughts and to use voting when making class decisions. This supports pupils to understand how citizens can influence decision-making through the democratic process. Smallberry Green currently holds the bronze award as a UNICEF Rights Respecting school and we are working towards the silver award.
The Rule of Law:
The school rules of ‘Ready, Respectful and Safe’ are embedded into the values of Smallberry Green. Pupils understand that the rules keep them safe and enable them to learn through a fair and consistent approach which ensures they successfully live and work together.
Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the police, fire service are regular parts of our calendar and help reinforce this message.
To encourage and promote good behaviour, attitude and work, we have adopted a behaviour system which is consistently followed throughout the school. We are committed to praising children’s efforts. We endeavour to praise the children informally, individually, during group work, in front of the whole class and school assemblies. Children are recognised not only for achievement in curriculum areas, but also for behaviour and demonstration of values. Children’s recognition takes the form of being put on the class recognition board and postcards or phone calls home.
Individual Liberty:
Through our curriculum, our PSHE lessons and through our assemblies, children are supported to understand their personal rights and freedoms. Pupils are actively encouraged to make choices at our school, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment Children are encouraged to raise ideas and to contribute to the life of the school.
Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our E-Safety teaching and PHSE education.
Smallberry Green has a robust anti-bullying culture and has in place a comprehensive Behaviour Policy, which has at its heart the freedom of all students to learn and grow safely.
Mutual Respect:
Respect underpins all that we do at Smallberry Green. It is truly embedded into the curriculum and the ethos of the school. We insist that all pupils, teachers, non-teaching staff and visitors to our school are treated with dignity and respect. This is expressed by all demonstrating good manners and fostering positive and professional relationships. Pupils learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with courtesy and respect and these values underpin all teaching and learning and all relationships in our school.
Tolerance of Those of Different Faiths and Beliefs:
Smallberry Green is situated in an area which is culturally diverse; therefore, we are committed to ensuring that children understand the cultures, faiths and beliefs of their friends and neighbours.
We promote that all children visit a range of places of worship and learn about different religious beliefs in our religious education lessons and assemblies. Beliefs, traditions and customs are studied and celebrated, reinforcing a deep understanding of British tolerance and acceptance of all cultures.
This is achieved through enhancing pupils’ understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity in our local community of Hounslow and London.
At Smallberry Green we will actively challenge pupils, staff or parents expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British Values, including ‘extremist’ views.

pageCache.text:
Head Teacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Smallberry Green Primary School’s website and we offer you a very warm welcome!
Smallberry Green is a happy, caring school with a strongly positive ethos and a genuinely friendly nature. We take real pride in the sense of community here, where every member of staff gets to know each child as an individual, encouraging them always to ‘be the best that they can be’. This shows in our children’s impeccable behaviour, built on being ‘ready, respectful and safe’ not only within the school building, but throughout the many extra-curricular experiences they take part in.
At Smallberry Green, we want every day to be an adventure. We believe exciting learning should happen everywhere, and we take real delight in creating memorable experiences for our children, both in and beyond the classroom.
Inside and out, our building is bright, spacious and full of life, supporting a rich, well-balanced curriculum that inspires and engages. Our classrooms, corridors and communal areas have recently been refurbished to create warm, inviting spaces where children can flourish. Our outdoor area is a real asset: an adobe hut, a field, football pitches, a basketball area, sheltered spaces for performing, climbing frames, bars, covered learning areas, tunnels, a sand-pit and much more.
We encourage families to be closely involved in their children’s learning, and we’re proud of our open communication with parents. We treasure the diverse cultural community within our school and celebrate it regularly through a range of events. Our children are taught to value resilience, optimism, respect, curiosity, inclusiveness and confidence, and we support families further through a variety of extra-curricular clubs, an early Breakfast Club and an After-School Club. Our commitment is unwavering: to help every child become a confident, respectful and successful global citizen, now and in the future.
At Smallberry Green, each of our pupils is ‘delightful’ in their own unique way, and we feel truly fortunate to be part of such a wonderful school community. We welcome you come and visit our school.

Smallberry Green Wrap-around Childcare
At Smallberry Green Primary School, our wrap-around childcare is operated and managed by the school. The staff who work in our wrap-around childcare work throughout the school and build strong relationships with the children in their care.
Our wrap-around childcare offers competitive childcare fees, high quality care and flexible booking, providing care for pupils from Nursery to Year 6. This provides parents/carers with the option of a convenient single drop-off from 7.30am and collection at 6pm.
Our vision is for all children to have fun! We aim to ensure children look forward to each and every session. Our wrap-around childcare supports and compliments our already rich curriculum by celebrating special weeks, festivals and days and incorporating activities such as arts and craft, cooking, outdoor and indoor games, reading, junk modelling, sand and water play and role-play. It is fully inclusive and accessible to all!
Our bespoke model of childcare and specialist club provision is unique because it enables families to mix and match childcare needs with a range of specialist club opportunities. Therefore, children can participate in an extra-curricular club and attend wrap-around care afterwards.
Our wrap-around care is inclusive and fully accessible to all children, including those with special educational needs, disabilities and those considered vulnerable.
Our Breakfast Club opens from 7.30am in the hall, offering pupils a nutritious and fun way to start the day. We provide the option of a tasty breakfast which consists of a variety of cereals, bagels/toast with spreads, fruit and milk. We encourage children to eat a good breakfast as we know it provides pupils with fuel for learning.
During this session, we offer a wide range of indoor play activities and team games. At the end of the session, our enthusiastic and friendly play-workers ensure all children get safely to their classes so they can participate in their soft start activities.
The club is open to all families from Nursery to Year 6. Regular and emergency sessions can be booked through Schoolcomms.
Our After School Club runs from the end of the school day until 6pm and is staffed by Smallberry Green’s fun and friendly playworkers.
We have a huge range of games, crafts and play experiences on offer, allowing children to express themselves, build confidence and make friends during each session. The club is based in the main hall with access to the playground and field.
During the session, a healthy afternoon snack is provided such as a crumpet, pitta bread, beans on toast, soup or pasta. A healthy snack aids growth and development and helps to establish healthy eating habits.
The club is open to all families from Nursery to Year 6. Regular and emergency sessions can be booked through Schoolcomms.
Our wrap-around childcare is competitively priced and offers excellent value for money.
Breakfast club is £6 per session booked in advance and £7 per session booked as an emergency
After-school club booked in advance is £6 from 3.15-4.30pm, £12 from 3.15-5.45pm and £13 from 3.15 until 6pm*
After-care booked as an emergency is £12 from 3.15 until 5.45pm only
*If you wish to use the provision until 6pm, please arrange this in advance with the aftercare team. A payment of £1 cash is payable on the day to the Aftercare team.
We promote and support government subsidies such as Tax-Free Childcare, Childcare vouchers and Universal Credit Childcare
Contact Details – If you have any queries regarding Wrap-around care at Smallberry Green, please contact the school office on 02085802070 or email office@smallberrygreen.hounslow.sch.uk – any of the office team will be more than happy to help you but Natalie Subeathar is the main point of contact.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum | The Smallberry Green Primary School, Turnpike Way Isleworth TW7 5BF
pageCache.text:
At Smallberry Green, the curriculum is intended to meet the needs of our wonderfully diverse community, ensuring all children’s backgrounds are celebrated and acknowledged. This is underpinned by an unwavering commitment, not only to achieve the highest academic standards but also to enable all of our children to become confident, respectful and successful global citizens in an ever-changing world now, and in the future. We do this through delivering a broad, well-balanced, subject led curriculum that is inspiring and engaging.
Our curriculum is inclusive and relevant to our diverse community. It ensures that each pupil develops the skills they need to succeed in the wider world. It has been designed to engage all learning styles and is relevant for all of our children, many of whom are new to English or have SEND. Carefully targeted support ensures children who may need extra help make excellent progress.
We fully recognise that parents and carers are critical partners in children’s learning journeys and we work closely with them through open sessions, workshops, newsletters, our website, fact sheets and other various forms of communication.
We are determined that all children develop strong language skills. Right from the start, there is a strong emphasis on early speaking and listening skills and phonics is embedded in all aspects of early school life. Reading throughout our curriculum is at the heart of everything we do. We promote a love of reading in all of our children by ensuring quality class texts are brought to life throughout our curriculum.
As well as reading, we have a strong emphasis on Maths, Writing and Science using the Maths Readiness Programme and carefully planned units of work.
We want to prepare our children for Secondary school and to recognise that each subject is incredibly important. We aim to create future authors, linguists, artists, inventors, mathematicians, sports-people, scientists, explorers, detectives and musicians etc. Consequently, all subjects are taught discretely. Where relevant, subjects may be linked together for children to make meaningful connections in their learning. Within all subjects there is a strong focus on vocabulary to ensure that children can not only read and write confidently but are able to discuss, debate and recall key information.
We also aim to ensure children develop interpersonal skills, build resilience and become creative, critical thinkers. Creativity is an integral part of our curriculum as we believe that there should be no limits to curiosity. We want all groups of children to develop a thirst for new experiences and knowledge. In order to give all of our children the experience of being creative, the school promotes regular musical events, performances, sports events, competitions and visitors into school. From Year 1, every child in the school learns a different musical instrument every year and all year groups benefit from receiving music lessons from a specialist. Our achievement in this area, has been acknowledged through the Music Mark.
We constantly provide enrichment opportunities to engage learning and believe that childhood should be a happy, investigative and enquiring time in children’s lives. Therefore, we plan a rich programme of fully inclusive clubs, trips, visits, visitors, community links and celebrations that bring classroom learning to real life and encompass awe and wonder. We make sure that these opportunities for children to have quality life experiences is part of each year group’s learning as we want our children to flourish in their areas of interest or skill.
We remain focused on developing and nurturing the whole child with a determination to teach all children the ways in which they can keep themselves safe through a strong PSCHE curriculum designed by Jigsaw and a wide array of well-being activities.
Curriculum Implementation
We use clear, focused, ‘skills-based learning steps’ and ‘steps to success’ as an effective tool in achieving intended learning outcomes, whilst ensuring that children retain knowledge learnt in different curriculum subjects.
Staff have had extensive training to enable them to use effective questioning techniques to develop higher order thinking skills, supporting them to challenge all learners. All lessons provide opportunities for learning skills as well as many recall and application activities to support the retention of knowledge and understanding in a broad, balanced and relevant curriculum. As well as this, we differentiate activities and resources accordingly and provide small group learning for different groups of children, as necessary.
At the heart of our curriculum is reading, writing, debate, discussion and maths. Where relevant subjects are linked to a key text or texts, which are brought alive with ‘wow days’ and ‘fabulous finishes’. In order to develop children’s oracy and confidence, we ensure that opportunities for speaking and listening are embedded throughout each child’s time in school.
Community involvement is an essential part of our curriculum and we celebrate local traditions and religious events throughout the year; including the celebration of different festivals where we involve parents wherever possible.
We ensure that all our children are happy, healthy and active. Our children’s enthusiasm for learning is highlighted by visitors to our school. This love of learning, begins in Early Years where a free flow, child focused learning environment stimulates the physical wellbeing of the children. Throughout the school, children are as active as possible making good use of our extensive outdoor area and equipment which has been acknowledged through our gold School Games award.
To supplement our offer, we also use the following published materials: Early Years Outcomes, National Curriculum Statutory Guidance, Sounds Write Phonics Programme, White Rose, Maths Mastery Readiness Programme, Rights Respecting Schools, RE – Widening Horizons, Get Set for PE, Charanga for music, Jigsaw for PSCHE and Switched On Computing.
Impact
Smallberry Green is an inclusive school where we celebrate the diversity of our children and families. We are very proud of our all our children, who make good personal progress across the curriculum and also in regards to our school values, self-confidence and resilience. Our children’s behaviour and attitudes really are ‘delightful’. (Ofsted 2018).
Throughout each child’s journey at Smallberry Green, they make at least good progress in relation to their different starting points in reading, writing and maths and develop secure knowledge understanding and skills across all subjects. We have high expectations and have a robust plan to ensure that more and more children, regardless of their starting points, make accelerated progress and achieve expected and exceeding standards across the curriculum.
Pupil voice shows us that children are passionate about their learning and enjoy coming to school. Children are increasingly able to recall key learning and discuss facts that they have learnt in different subjects.
Each and every child at Smallberry Green is an individual with different starting points, on a different learning journey and with different strengths and areas to develop. Our curriculum, teaching and learning and nurturing environment ensures that each child achieves their personal best during their time with us.
Children leave our school with a sense of belonging to a tightly knit community where they have the confidence and skills to make decisions, self-evaluate, make connections and become life-long global learners.

Online Safety
What is online safety?
This is is the safe use of the internet for gaming and communication. It included devices such as laptops, tablets, smartphones and games consoles. It is important that children and young people understand the benefits, risks and responsibilities of using and sharing information online.
Children are taught about online safety in the PSHE curriculum and Computing curriculum.
Mr Masters has prepared a presentation with tips for children and families on how to stay safe online.
Keeping Children Safe Online
Using the Internet safely at home
While many Internet Service Providers (ISPs) offer filtering systems to help you safeguard your child at home, it remains surprisingly easy for children to access inappropriate material including unsuitable texts, pictures and movies. Parents are advised to set the security levels within Internet browsers with this in mind. Locating the computer or tablet in a family area, not a bedroom, will enable you to supervise children as they use the Internet. However, don’t deny your child the opportunity to learn from the wide variety of material and games available on the Internet. Instead, set some simple rules for keeping them safe and make sure they understand the importance of these rules.
Simple rules for keeping your child safe
To keep your child safe they should:
only email and message people they know
Using these rules
Go through the rules with your child. It is also a good idea to regularly check the Internet sites your child is visiting e.g. by clicking on History and Favourites. Please reassure your child that you want to keep them safe rather than take Internet access away from them.
Stay switched on campaign
This campaign from ‘internet matters’ aims to remind parents to “stay switched on” around issues their children might be facing, including cyberbullying, screen time, peer pressure, online grooming and viewing inappropriate content.
Find out more here: https://www.internetmatters.org/
Talking to your children about staying safe online
We regularly use our RSHE lessons to remind your children about the importance of staying safe online. You can use some of the resources below to continue the conversation.
Ofsted have produced a useful ‘Online Safety Webinar’ for parents and schools. The webinar focuses on the work of the Breck Foundation. This foundation is a self-funding charity, raising awareness of playing safe whilst using the internet. It was established following the death of a young boy called Breck who was groomed online.
The webinar lasts for around 1 hour. For parents who are short on time we would recommend that the first 23 minutes are watched, after that Ofsted focus on what schools and inspectors can do to keep children safe.
